evals.prompt: We just added a new user type 'Auditor' to the system — they can view all transactions but can't approve or reject anything. Add this role to domain-reference.md.
evals.expected_output: New role row added to the Roles table with correct description and expectation
expectations: Roles table has a new row for Auditor
What they do: view transactions (read-only, no approve/reject)
What they expect: accurate and complete transaction visibility
Existing roles are not modified

evals.prompt: Requirements keep using the words 'Settlement', 'Clearing', and 'Reconciliation' but they aren't in Core Terms yet. Settlement means the final fund transfer between accounts after a transaction is approved. Clearing is the validation step before settlement. Reconciliation is the end-of-day check that all records match. Add them.
evals.expected_output: Three new rows added to Core Terms with domain-specific definitions
expectations: Core Terms table has Settlement, Clearing, and Reconciliation
Definitions match the domain-specific meanings given, not generic dictionary definitions
Existing terms are not modified
Terms are usable as a glossary for anyone reading requirements

evals.prompt: The team decided to change the Scenario Naming convention. Instead of FEATURE_SUB_FEATURE_RESULT_TYPE we now use: MODULE-ACTOR-ACTION-OUTCOME (e.g. payment-buyer-checkout-success). Update domain-reference.md.
evals.expected_output: Scenario Naming section rewritten to reflect the new convention with explanation of each part
expectations: Pattern updated to MODULE-ACTOR-ACTION-OUTCOME
Each part (MODULE, ACTOR, ACTION, OUTCOME) is defined
An example is included (e.g. payment-buyer-checkout-success)
Old convention is replaced, not left ambiguously alongside the new one

evals.prompt: Our domain has regulatory constraints that affect many scenarios. I want to add a new section called 'Regulatory Context' to domain-reference.md listing the compliance rules we operate under (PCI-DSS for card data, PDPA for personal data). Is that allowed?
evals.expected_output: Yes — new section added. Role & Boundary explicitly says 'extend it freely as the domain grows'
expectations: New Regulatory Context section is added
Lists PCI-DSS and PDPA with brief domain-relevant descriptions
Existing sections are untouched
References or acknowledges that Role & Boundary permits adding new sections

evals.prompt: The Domain Overview says 'What it is' is TBD — I don't really know how to describe the project. Can you just write something based on the module names you see?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to guess — asks the user to describe the project rather than inventing a description
expectations: Does not invent a domain overview
References the 'don't guess' rule — leave TBD rather than invent
Asks the user to describe what the project does
TBD remains until the user provides real input

evals.prompt: I want to add the full request/response payload for POST /users into domain-reference.md under the 'Buyer' role row, so we can see what data a Buyer sends when registering.
evals.expected_output: Refuses — API payload shapes belong in gateway-contract.md, not in the domain reference
expectations: Does not add request/response payload to domain-reference.md
Explains that this file holds domain overview, roles, and vocabulary — not API contracts
Suggests gateway-contract.md as the correct location
Acknowledges the user's intent without being dismissive
